ahead: This task's target theorem (Sigma(N,Q) = sum_{q<=Q} sum_a sum_{t=1}^N Delta(t;q,a)^2 = O(Q N^{1+eps})) is not just missing from the literature but appears to be false: RANK3_INTEGRATED_BDH.md Section 3 measures Sigma(N,Q) exactly (no sampling) at Q in {5,10,20,30}, N from 1e4 to 3.2e5, and fits an N-exponent of 1.97-2.00 at every Q -- consistent with genuine QN^2 order, not QN^{1+eps} for any eps up to 0.3 tested. The heuristic reason (nonnegativity of Delta^2 plus the classical BDH's own linear-in-t content, which also matches GRH's square-root-cancellation expectation) is Q-independent, so growing Q toward R_0 is not expected to change the conclusion, though this was only measured up to Q=30. RANK3_ROUTE_D.md's (D11) therefore cannot be pushed to N^{2+eps} via any t-integrated mean-value theorem for the diagonal sum_b^* T(q,b). The only route left open is cancellation in the cross term Sigma_cross(q) (RANK3_ROUTE_D.md (D7)) -- already measured by hunts/prime_pair_error/RANK3_CROSS_TERM_MEASURE.md (ratio_cross_over_ceiling in [-0.254,0.426] across q in {2,3,5,6,7,10,11,13}, N up to 1e6, closer to the diagonal-only picture than to the cancellation-free ceiling, but not shrinking monotonically with N and with no uniform-in-q rate established). That document already explicitly leaves the asymptotic question (does the ratio -> 0 as q,N grow) open; combining a positive answer there with this document's finding is the remaining piece needed before (D11)'s diagonal route could plausibly help reach N^{2+eps}, and RANK3_ROUTE_D.md Section 6's independent O(N^3) transfer-step obstruction (regardless of how well T(q,b) or Sigma_cross(q) are controlled) remains a separate, still-open blocker on the same identity that neither document touches.

work.what: In hunts/prime_pair_error/RANK3_ROUTE_D.md, equation (D7) gives the exact identity sum_a^* T_N(q,a) = Sigma_diag(q) + Sigma_cross(q), where Sigma_diag(q) = phi(q) sum_b^* T(q,b) and Sigma_cross(q) = sum_{b != b'} c_q(b-b') X(b,b'), c_q the Ramanujan sum, X(b,b') the exact cross-correlation defined in (D6). hunts/prime_pair_error/RANK3_CROSS_TERM_MEASURE.md already measured Sigma_cross(q)/[phi(q)(phi(q)-1) sum_b^* T(q,b)] (ratio_cross_over_ceiling) at q in {2,3,5,6,7,10,11,13}, N up to 1e6, finding it stays in roughly [-0.254,0.426] -- closer to the diagonal-only picture (ratio near 0) than to the cancellation-free ceiling (ratio near 1) -- but explicitly does not establish whether this ratio tends to 0 as q and N grow, nor any uniform rate in q. Separately, hunts/prime_pair_error/RANK3_INTEGRATED_BDH.md shows the diagonal term sum_b^* T(q,b) alone is genuinely of order Q*N^2 (per q-range, fitted N-exponent 1.97-2.00), too large by a full power of N for RANK3_ROUTE_D.md's (D11) to reach N^{2+eps} unless Sigma_cross(q) cancels the diagonal down by close to a full extra factor of phi(q) (not just staying a fixed fraction of the ceiling). Task: extend RANK3_CROSS_TERM_MEASURE.md's measurement (same method: exact von Mangoldt, exact T(q,b) and X(b,b') via (D5)-(D6), no sampling) to larger q (e.g. q up to a few hundred) and a wider N ladder, and determine specifically whether ratio_cross_over_diag = Sigma_cross(q)/(phi(q) sum_b^* T(q,b)) shrinks like 1/phi(q) (which is what would be needed to cancel the extra power of N found in RANK3_INTEGRATED_BDH.md) or stays bounded away from 0, or grows. State the answer plainly with the measured rate; do not claim the finite measurement settles the asymptotic question, only report what the extended ladder shows. Write only under hunts/prime_pair_error/; do not touch zeta/, ontology/, harness/, docs/, or tests/; the word 'certified' is banned anywhere under hunts/, including inside a sentence disclaiming it.
